items.q: and I signed the contract with the man, but Billy Berg, you know, he was very fond of me

ctx.x: and open with us, because you know, you want to play with this big band." And everybody wanted to play with a big band, and everybody wanted to play with Duke Ellington, you know, so I had told them that it was my opening night, that my name was out front, Lee and Lester Young. I said, "I'm gonna go play with Duke tonight; you'll have to get another drummer." And he said, "What do you mean? You're the leader!"

I said, "I don't care. I may not ever get a chance to play with Duke in my life, and I'm not gonna give this up." You know, and I signed the contract with the man, but Billy Berg, you know, he was very fond of me, you know - he had to be, because he says, "You've got to be the craziest man in the world. How can you be the leader of the band and you're not gonna make your opening?" And I said, "There's no need talking about it; I'm going to go play with Duke tonight." I always wanted to know how he started the…

You know how you start playing the piano, and all of a sudden, here comes the band - BANG, you know, and that was always a mystery to me, that I wanted solved. And so I said, "I'm gonna go play with him." And I left him, and I left him and I played the Trianon with Duke and them that night. Luckily, when I came back the next night, I still had a job, but you know, it was only because the man liked me. Because, you know, that was a little far out.
